en: The Questions of King Milinda:
The Chapter on Similes, Part One:
The Section on the Earth.
2. The Question on Water “Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you say—that ‘five qualities of water should be adopted’—which are those five qualities that should be adopted?
“Just as water, O King, is well-settled, unshaken, undisturbed, and pure by nature;”

"In the same way, Great King, the yogin, the practitioner of yoga, having removed hypocrisy, flattery, hinting, and belittling, must possess conduct that is well-established, unshakable, undisturbed, and pure by nature.
This, Great King, is the first quality of water to be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, water is established in its nature of coolness."

In the same way, great king, a practitioner of yoga, a follower of the spiritual life, should be endowed with patience, loving-kindness, and compassion toward all beings, seeking their welfare and being sympathetic.
This, great king, is the second quality of water that should be adopted.
Furthermore, great king, water makes the impure pure.

In the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, whether in the village or in the forest, must be free from legal disputes and act without omission toward his preceptor and those who are like preceptors, and toward his teacher and those who are like teachers.
This, great king, is the third quality of water that should be adopted.
Furthermore, great king, water is sought after by many people.

In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, a follower of the holy life, should be one who has few desires, is contented, secluded, withdrawn, and constantly aspires for the welfare of the entire world.
This, Great King, is the fourth quality of water that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, water does not bring harm to anyone.

In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga who is devoted to the practice should not commit any evil through body, speech, or mind that produces quarrels, strife, contention, disputes, or the arising of distress in others.
This, Great King, is the fifth quality of water that should be adopted.
And this, Great King, was spoken by the Blessed One, the God beyond Gods, in the Kaṇha Jātaka:
“If you would grant me a boon, O Sakka,
Lord of all beings,
let neither my mind nor my body [be subject to decay].”
“O Sakka, may no one ever be harmed on my account; this,
Sakka, is the boon I choose.”
The second question on the corner of the eye.
